# Entity reference

Every entity class that ships with the addon, grouped by what you use it for. Each entry lists its inputs, its outputs, and its keys with their defaults. Arguments in brackets are what an input accepts or an output passes along. [[io-concepts]] explains how the pieces connect.

A few things hold for all of them. Every entity with I/O has a `targetname`, except `logic_auto` which has no properties. Key values are converted to int, float, bool, Vector3 or Color based on the FGD defaults and missing keys get the defaults listed here. Distances are in map units (32 to a meter) unless marked otherwise; `omni_range`, `spot_range` and `max_distance` are in meters. The input and output lists are what the editor offers in its pickers, but any public method on the script works as an input at runtime.

The definitions themselves live in `crates/gt_formats/src/builtin_entities.json`. The Godot copies in `addons/func_godot/fgd/godottrench` are generated from it, and a test keeps the two in sync.

## Logic

Logic entities have no body and no visuals. They sit in the map as small markers and exist to shape the flow of signals: relaying, counting, branching, timing and sequencing.

### logic_relay

The basic building block. It forwards whatever triggers it, and can be switched off, so it is also the easiest way to make a chain that only works under some condition.

Inputs
: `trigger(activator)`, `enable`, `disable`, `toggle`
Outputs
: `triggered(activator)`
Keys
: `start_disabled` 0

### logic_branch

Remembers a true or false value and fires one of two outputs when tested. Use it for "only if the power is on" style checks.

Inputs
: `set_true`, `set_false`, `toggle`, `test`, `set_and_test(value)`
Outputs
: `on_true`, `on_false`
Keys
: `start_value` 0

### logic_counter

Counts up and down between a minimum and maximum, for "press all three buttons" puzzles. The value is clamped, and outputs only fire when it actually changes. `reset` only fires `changed`.

Inputs
: `add(amount)` (1 by default), `subtract(amount)`, `set_value(value)`, `reset`
Outputs
: `hit_max`, `hit_min`, `changed(value)`
Keys
: `min` 0, `max` 3, `start_value` 0

### logic_timer

Fires `timer` every interval. Set `random_max` above `random_min` to pick a random interval each time instead. It runs from the moment the map loads unless `start_on` is 0.

Inputs
: `start`, `stop`, `toggle`, `fire` (fires once, now)
Outputs
: `timer`
Keys
: `interval` 1.0, `random_min` 0, `random_max` 0, `start_on` 1, `once` 0

### logic_auto

Fires `map_spawn` once, just after the map is ready. It is the place to start anything that should run from the beginning.

Outputs
: `map_spawn`

### logic_sequence

Fires up to eight numbered steps in order, waiting before each one, including the first. `times` sets the waits per step as a space separated list, steps without an entry use `interval`. With `loop` on it starts over and never fires `finished`. `start` is ignored while it runs, and `stop` followed by `start` begins again from step 1.

Inputs
: `start`, `stop`, `reset`
Outputs
: `step_1` to `step_8`, `step(index)`, `finished`
Keys
: `steps` 3 (1 to 8), `interval` 1.0, `times` empty, `start_active` 0, `loop` 0

### logic_script

Runs a snippet of GDScript when fired, for the one piece of logic that no combination of inputs expresses, such as reading the player's health. `source` is compiled once when the map loads. In scope are `this`, `activator`, `parameter`, `io` (the `GodotTrenchIO` class) and `tree`. Indent nested lines with tabs, spaces give mixed indentation and the snippet fails to compile. `run_with` always has a null `activator`.

Inputs
: `run(activator)`, `run_with(parameter)`
Outputs
: `ran(result)`
Keys
: `source` empty, `expression` empty (used when `source` is empty)

### logic_call

Calls a method on any node with fixed arguments, for reaching game code such as a score autoload. A `"$parameter"` element in `arguments` is replaced with the incoming parameter. Unlike plain outputs, it warns when the target does not exist.

Inputs
: `trigger(activator)`, `call_with(parameter)`
Outputs
: `called(result)`
Keys
: `call_target` `/root/Game`, `method` empty, `arguments` `[]`

### logic_debug

Prints a line when it receives an input, and optionally shows it as a label in debug builds. With `trace_all` on it logs every output in the game, which is a quick way to watch a whole chain.

Inputs
: `write(parameter, activator)`, `toggle`
Outputs
: `printed(text)`
Keys
: `message` "{name} received {parameter} from {activator}" (also `{time}`), `show_label` 1, `trace_all` 0

### logic_animate

Plays animations on the first `AnimationPlayer` at or under `target`, so I/O can drive a character or prop that carries its own animations. `target` can be `!activator`, which plays the animation on whoever started the chain.

Inputs
: `play(name)`, `stop`, `queue(name)`, `seek(time)`
Outputs
: `finished(anim)`
Keys
: `target` `!self`, `animation` empty, `speed` 1.0

## Doors, movers and buttons

These are brush entities: draw the brush, then convert it. They move by animating their body, so they carry players standing on them. Speeds are in meters per second, or degrees per second for rotation. None of them react to the player on their own, your player calls `use(activator)` on them, see [[button-door-example]].

### func_door

Slides by `travel` when opened. With `wait` at -1 it stays open, a positive value closes it again after that many seconds. A locked door ignores `open` and `use` and fires `locked_use` instead.

Inputs
: `open`, `close`, `toggle`, `lock`, `unlock`, `use(activator)`
Outputs
: `opened`, `closed`, `started_opening`, `started_closing`, `locked_use(activator)`
Keys
: `travel` 0 64 0, `speed` 2.0, `wait` -1, `locked` 0, `start_open` 0, `interact` 1

### func_door_rotating

Swings around a hinge, which you can drag in the viewport. `open_away` makes it swing away from whoever opens it, which is why `open` takes the activator here.

Inputs
: `open(activator)`, `close`, `toggle(activator)`, `lock`, `unlock`, `use(activator)`
Outputs
: same as func_door
Keys
: `hinge` 0 0 0 (relative to the door), `axis` y, `open_angle` 95, `speed` 120, `open_away` 1, `wait` -1, `locked` 0, `start_open` 0, `interact` 1

### func_gate

A rotating door with fewer options, for gates and simple swinging panels. It runs the same script as func_door_rotating.

Inputs
: `open`, `close`, `toggle`
Outputs
: `opened`, `closed`
Keys
: `hinge`, `open_angle` 100, `speed` 90

### func_platform

Moves between its start and `start + travel`. `mode` 0 goes one way per toggle, 1 ping pongs with `wait` seconds at each end, 2 goes once.

Inputs
: `start`, `stop`, `toggle`, `go_to_end`, `go_to_start`
Outputs
: `reached_end`, `reached_start`, `started`
Keys
: `travel` 0 128 0, `speed` 2.0, `wait` 1.0, `mode` 0, `start_active` 0

### func_train

Follows a chain of `path_corner` entities, starting at `target`. It moves from the moment the map loads and loops, so set `start_active` or `loop` to 0 for a one off ride.

Inputs
: `start`, `stop`, `toggle`
Outputs
: `arrived(corner)`, `finished` (only when not looping)
Keys
: `target`, `speed` 3.0, `loop` 1, `start_active` 1, `orient` 0

### func_button

Moves by `travel` while pressed and fires `pressed`. With `wait` at -1 it stays pressed.

Inputs
: `press(activator)`, `release`, `lock`, `unlock`, `use(activator)`
Outputs
: `pressed(activator)`, `released`, `locked_use(activator)`
Keys
: `travel` 0 -2 0, `wait` 1.0, `locked` 0, `interact` 1
`interact` 0 disables `use` on doors and buttons without affecting their other inputs, for doors that only open from a trigger or a script.

## Triggers

Triggers are invisible brush volumes that react to physics bodies entering them. `filter_group` limits them to members of a Godot group, `player` by default, and an empty value accepts any body. Most of them share these inputs and outputs:

Inputs
: `enable`, `disable`, `toggle`
Outputs
: `triggered(activator)`, `entered(activator)`, `exited(activator)`
Keys
: `filter_group` player, `start_disabled` 0

`entered` fires on every accepted entry, `triggered` respects the cooldown, and `exited` fires even while the trigger is disabled. The cooldown is tracked per body, so two players entering close together each still fire it, one waiting on the other's cooldown does not hold it up.

### trigger_once

Fires once and disables itself. The `enable` input arms it again.

### trigger_multiple

Fires on every entry, at most once per `cooldown`, 0.5 seconds by default.

### trigger_hurt

Damages bodies inside it by calling their `take_damage(amount, source)`, `damage * interval` per tick. Its `filter_group` is empty by default, so it hurts everything, not just the player. `hurt` only fires for a body that actually took damage, meaning it has a `take_damage` method, or for any accepted body when `filter_group` names a group.

Outputs
: `hurt(activator)`, per damaged body per tick
Keys
: `damage` 10 per second, `damage_method` take_damage, `interval` 0.5, `filter_group` empty

### trigger_teleport

Moves bodies to the `info_teleport_destination` named in `destination`, taking its position and facing, and stops them unless `keep_velocity` is 1.

Outputs
: `teleported(activator)`
Keys
: `destination`, `filter_group` player, `keep_velocity` 0, `cooldown` 0.5

### trigger_push

Pushes bodies with `push`, in map units per second. With `once` at 1 each entry gets one impulse, at 0 it pushes steadily, like a wind tunnel, firing `pushed` once when a body enters rather than every frame. A rigid body being pushed stops accelerating once it reaches `push` speed, it does not keep gaining speed past it.

Outputs
: `pushed(activator)`
Keys
: `push` 0 384 0, `filter_group` empty, `once` 1

### trigger_call

Calls a method when triggered, on `!activator` by default, so a trigger can call straight into the player's script.

Inputs
: `trigger(activator)` and the shared inputs
Outputs
: `called(result)` and the shared outputs
Keys
: `call_target` `!activator`, `method`, `arguments` `[]`, `once` 0, `cooldown` 0.5

### trigger_spawn_area

Spawns scenes inside its volume, by default when the player enters. Works like info_spawner below. `toggle` starts or stops the spawn timer.

Inputs
: `spawn`, `start`, `stop`, `toggle`, `kill_all`
Outputs
: `spawned(node)`, `all_dead`, `exhausted` (fires once, the first time `total` is reached)
Keys
: `scene`, `count` 3, `max_alive` 10, `total` 0, `interval` 0, `spawn_on_enter` 1, `filter_group` player, `spawn_group` enemies, `snap_to_ground` 1, `cooldown` 0.5

## Actors, props and effects

These are point entities.

### info_spawner

Spawns a scene around itself, up to `max_alive` at a time and `total` overall (0 means unlimited). Spawned nodes join `spawn_group` and are added next to the spawner. They have no targetname, so reach them with `@enemies` or whatever group you chose.

Inputs
: `spawn`, `start`, `stop`, `toggle`, `kill_all`
Outputs
: `spawned(node)`, `all_dead`, `exhausted` (fires once, the first time `total` is reached)
Keys
: `scene`, `count` 1, `max_alive` 5, `total` 0, `interval` 0, `radius` 64, `start_active` 0, `spawn_on_ready` 0, `spawn_group` enemies, `snap_to_ground` 1

### info_teleport_destination

Marks where trigger_teleport sends things. Only has a `targetname`.

### path_corner

One stop on a path, with `target` naming the next. Trains and walkers fire its `reached` output when they arrive.

Outputs
: `reached(train)`
Keys
: `target`, `wait` 0, `speed` 0 (trains only)

### npc_walker

A scripted actor that walks a chain of path corners playing animations, for cutscenes rather than AI. It moves by tweening its position, with no gravity or collision, and `face` and `walk_to` accept any target selector, so `face` with the parameter `!player` turns it towards the player.

Inputs
: `start`, `stop`, `walk_to(corner)`, `play_anim(name)`, `face(target)`
Outputs
: `arrived(corner)`, `reached_goal`, `finished`
Keys
: `model`, `target`, `speed` 2.0, `loop` 0, `start_active` 0, `walk_anim` walk, `idle_anim` idle, `face_travel` 1

### game_text

Shows a line of text in the world, on the HUD or both. `show` and `hide` toggle the label, not the node. The world label draws on top of everything, so it is visible through walls.

Inputs
: `show`, `hide`, `set_text(text)`, `flash(seconds)`
Outputs
: `shown`, `hidden`
Keys
: `text`, `place` world, hud or both, `start_visible` 0, `duration` 0, `text_color` 255 255 255, `world_size` 0.01

### prop_physics

A physics prop that can be thrown, damaged and broken, like crates and barrels. Enough damage, a hard enough impact or `smash` breaks it, and an explosive prop blasts when it breaks, after its `fuse` if it was ignited. `broken` fires after the blast, so whatever it triggers already sees the damage.

Inputs
: `smash`, `ignite(activator)`, `push(direction)`, `take_damage(amount, source)`
Outputs
: `damaged(hp)`, `broken`
Keys
: `model`, `size` 16 16 16 (half extents), `mass` 5.0, `health` 30, `explosive` 0, `explosion_radius` 192, `explosion_damage` 40, `fuse` 0.6, `impact_speed` 0, `debris_scene`

### prop_model

A static model with optional collision, for props that should not move.

Keys
: `model` (.bbmodel, .glb, .gltf or .tscn), `collision` convex (or none, trimesh), `scale` 1.0

### env_explosion

On `explode`, damages every node in the scene within `radius` by `damage * (1 - distance / radius)` and pushes rigid bodies away. Distance is measured to each node's origin, with no line of sight check. The blast is spatial, so it also reaches nodes outside the map, such as a player added next to the `FuncGodotMap`.

Inputs
: `explode(activator)`
Outputs
: `exploded`
Keys
: `radius` 256, `damage` 50, `force` 8, `damage_method` take_damage, `effect_scene`

### light and light_spot

Switchable omni and spot lights. `switched` only fires when the state actually changes.

Inputs
: `turn_on`, `turn_off`, `toggle`
Outputs
: `switched(on)`
Keys
: `light_energy` 1.0 (1.5 for spots), `light_color`, `start_on` 1, and `omni_range` 10, or `spot_range` 15 and `spot_angle` 35

### env_sound

A positional sound. `max_distance` 0 means no limit.

Inputs
: `play`, `stop`, `toggle`
Outputs
: `finished`
Keys
: `sound`, `volume_db` 0, `max_distance` 0, `autoplay_on` 0, `loop_sound` 0

### env_particles

A particle effect for smoke, fire, sparks and dust. `burst` fires one shot.

Inputs
: `start`, `stop`, `toggle`, `burst`
Keys
: `amount` 32, `lifetime` 2.0, `one_shot` 0, `start_emitting` 0

## Not in the library

The plain FuncGodot classes, `worldspawn`, `func_geo`, `func_detail`, `func_detail_illusionary` and `func_illusionary`, come from the base definition file. Worldspawn holds the map's sun, ambient light, sky, fog and streaming settings, and the Inspector shows it when nothing is selected.

`info_player_start` and `trigger_area` are known to the editor but only defined by the demo project. If you use them in your own project, add definitions for them, or they build as plain nodes with a warning.

The player is not an entity either. The library expects it to be in the `player` group, on collision layer 1, and to have a `take_damage(amount, source)` method. `godot/demo/player.gd` is a complete example.
